title: docs(audits): the #4001 strictness campaign's closing record — terminal re-measure, one instrument start to final
body:
Part of #4001 — the campaign anchor stays open. Its closure is a PM/maintainer decision taken after this lands, deliberately not triggered here: #8687 carries a `Blocked-by:` on the anchor that needs re-pricing at closure time.

## What this is

The campaign's **terminal re-measure**: re-run the site census on the final tree, confirm the three closing claims, and write the closing record into the ledger. Measurement and record only — **no schema changed, no `.zod.ts` touched, no `FormFieldBaseSchema` touched**. The diff is two hunks of prose in one audit doc.

## The census found ZERO drift, so the generated artifact does not move

`gen:strictness-ledger` reproduces the committed counts **byte-for-byte** on today's `main` — `git status` clean after regeneration. Worth stating plainly because the dispatch assumed the closing record would be "prose + regenerated counts": on this tree the regeneration is a no-op, and that is the result, not a skipped step. Nothing under the five triaged directories has moved since 批 20 landed (verified: zero `packages/spec/src/**/*.zod.ts` in `c308a4f..origin/main`).

## The three closing claims, confirmed against `origin/main`

1. **Global authorable strip = exactly 1**, and it is ui/`FormFieldBaseSchema` (`view.zod.ts:1888`). Bucket split: `authorable 1 · unresolved 0 · wire/open 118 · no door 3 · no gate 0 · covered 1` = 123. Only `ui/` contributes; `data/` / `automation/` / `security/` / `studio/` all read 0. The other five `ui/` strip sites resolve per their rows — `ViewItemWireSchema` ×2 wire, `BaseNavItemSchema` covered, `FieldWidgetPropsSchema` no door, `ActionSessionSchema` wire.
2. **`data/`'s forced scope is discharged** — authorable bucket 0 across its 81 remaining strip sites, every one carrying a wire/open/no-door verdict and a row.
3. **`data/object.zod.ts` is shut** — 批 20's unit is the file's 14 inner blocks (13 + the held `IndexSchema`); the AST unit is 20 object sites, **all 20 strict, 0 strip**. Both readings are recorded, because a future reader comparing "14/14" against a generated "20" should not have to re-derive that they are different units of one fact.

## One premise of the campaign's own opening post did not survive

**The start and final numbers were never comparable, because the instrument changed underneath them.** #4001's opening triple (`.strict()=31 / .passthrough()=20 / strip=1885`) was taken with the **textual** method that `scripts/lib/strictness-ledger.ts` later documented as wrong in both directions. Publishing today's AST reading against it would report an instrument change as a campaign result — this file's own subject matter.

So the record re-takes the start column with **today's** instrument, over the campaign's start tree (`d6bfb3d0a`, `main`'s tip when #4001 was filed). Both columns are one instrument:

| triaged five | Sites | strict | passthrough | strip |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| start (2026-07-30) | 484 | 12 | 4 | **468** |
| final (2026-08-16) | 439 | 310 | 6 | **123** |

Two things fall out, both recorded:

- On the start tree the AST reads **15** strict where the post recorded 31, and the post's per-directory table under-read `ui/` 177→183, `data/` 149→157, `system/` 383→389. The campaign's forced scope was planned as **"≈453 authorable sites"**; the AST says **484**. The plan was drawn against a number that was never measured, low by more than the whole of `studio/`.
- **The site total FELL by 45.** `strip 468 → 123` is two movements summed: shapes tightened, and shapes retired under ADR-0049 because the per-schema read came back "nobody writes this". The campaign's most common outcome of reading a shape carefully was *not* tightening it.

(Getting this required deepening the container's shallow clone — its history reached back only to 2026-08-15, so the start tree was initially unreachable.)

## The parked entry, and why the campaign can end with it open

`FormFieldBaseSchema` is a module-private base with zero `.parse()` of its own; its sole consumer is the door — `FormFieldBaseSchema.extend({ fields }).strict().transform(…)` — so an undeclared form-field key is already refused with the ADR-0089 visibility map. It stays `authorable` rather than `covered` because #5249's separating test is mechanical: `covered` needs a `...X.shape` **spread** (which makes the base inert); this consumer uses `.extend()`, which **inherits** posture, so the base is a real door whose posture is overridden downstream. The record states the **restart condition** and shows it is gated rather than remembered: `view-strictness-batch18.test.ts` goes red if the consumer's `.strict()` is dropped, and `check:strictness-ledger` stops the site leaving the map quietly.

The record also names the four mechanisms that hold the posture now that no batch is scheduled — the ledger gate, the reverse pin at zero, the `strictObject` template, and the unknown-key warning layer — and answers the standing question in "Next steps" §1 with "still nothing", as that step explicitly asks whoever reads it next to do.

## Second hunk, declared: a stale worklist bullet the record would otherwise stand over

"Next steps" §3's `BaseNavItemSchema` bullet still read **"Still open."** and stated the **wrong mechanism** (that the union members `.extend()` the base; they spread `...shape` — that difference is the whole of finding 16). It was settled by the #5249 ruling as `covered`. Left in place, the closing record would certify a campaign as finished directly above a worklist item claiming it is not. Struck rather than deleted, per this file's own convention, with the correction and a pointer to the `app.zod.ts` row that carries the evidence. Same defect class as the slice (ledger record accuracy), mechanical, and the correct form was already pinned by that row.

## Verification — union re-run at final head `abaf62009`

- **`check:strictness-ledger` green** at `abaf62009`: 61 files / 5 triaged dirs, 22 open files / 123 strip sites, counts current, **1 authorable strip site left**.
- **Reverse verification, both halves, predicted direction observed.**
  - *The census is a live reading of the tree, and the parked site is genuinely the sole authorable one*: mutating `FormFieldBaseSchema` to `z.strictObject(` **on a scratch copy of `src/`** takes global strip 123 → 122 and drops exactly that entry from the `ui/` strip list. Run on a copy on purpose — the slice's prohibition on touching any `.zod.ts` is absolute, and `git status` stayed clean throughout.
  - *The gate is live over this commit*: hand-patching the counts' authorable bucket 1 → 0 exits 1 with the stale-artifact message; restored from `HEAD`, byte-identical, green again.
- **`check:generated` 13/13** (incl. `check:docs` — **zero generated reference-page drift**, as the dispatch predicted; plus `check:authorable-surface`, `check:api-surface`, `check:migration-registry`), after building the spec closure.
- **Diff-derived union** via `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs`: `check:doc-authoring` (376 files clean) and `check:doc-formula-expressions` (1408 TS blocks + 9 spec TSDoc examples) — both green. ⚠️ Reported honestly: `check:doc-authoring`'s own self-test prints that `docs/{audits,handoff,plans}` are **out of its scope**, so the derivation named a gate that does not actually cover this diff. It ran and is green; it is not evidence about this change.
- **`check:nul-bytes`** green (5969 files), plus a self-scan of the changed file for control bytes — clean.
- **No changeset**, per the measured repo convention rather than a rule recalled: PR #8563 — this same ledger, this same campaign, `docs/audits`-only — carried no changeset and the `skip-changeset` label. Applied here. (The repo's changeset gate has no path-based exemption; the label is the only one, so it is a real step rather than a declaration.)

Out of scope and untouched: every `.zod.ts`, `FormFieldBaseSchema` itself, the 22 non-authorable strip rows, `content/docs/releases/**`. #8687 is not addressed here and remains open; #8562 remains open.
